book.Title: PVT-LOG - LEAD PROF - E.01
book.page:
USERS: DR. AFRON NIELST - LEAD SCIENCE OFFICER MESSAGE HISTORY - XX-XX-XXXX CO--UROTPIE-D -- [DATE ... UNKNOWN] =====================================================================
I awoke this morning to a message in my inbox, we've been greenlit to move on with the final stages of Project LIEF.
Finally, a moment of true exposure for my recent experiments. A moment to be vindicated and recognized for the truly revolutionary deeds I've done here.

We've, with my guidance of course, synthesized several key compounds that hold the mechanisms neccesary to biological unlockings so incredible, that flesh might finally revere thought.
If we can perfect this solution, we can create a tonic that when taken, allows one to sculpt themselves with their very minds.
The only thing holding me back, are the nitwits they assigned me. Sure Dr. ######### has some genius when it comes to her ... its ... however that thing refers to themselves, chemical synthesis skills. But they're a bit too ... altruistic? Humble? All 'hypothetical trials before clinical trials.'
What a child.

Science Officer Yoltum's a lazy bum, doing only what they are told and not putting in the effort to explore beyond their ability. Ignorant boy.
Assistant Science Officer Xeveye is ... tolerable. They praise my incredible genius--as they should--and speak with utmost respect while in my presence and presumably outside of it as well. He's a bit naive. But, I'll allow his presence for now.

The rest of the crew are a bunch of fools. Drabble, empty heads that only follow directions. But I'll make use of this lot. My road to glory was paved with agonies, but it was worth it. It was worth the wait, the time, the sweat, the blood. The humiliation at the hands of this society.
I will be the herald of a new era.

book.Title: PVT-LOG - LEAD PROF - E.02
book.page:
USERS: DR. AFRON NIELST - LEAD SCIENCE OFFICER MESSAGE HISTORY - XX-XX-XXXX CO--UROTPIE-D -- [DATE ... UNKNOWN] =====================================================================
Dr. ########, all dour-eyed, whining like a sheep over the "dangers" of the clinical experiments. We've kept our biosynthization methods within scope. Somewhat. And though yes some of the recent clinical test on the vermin have resulted in, how shall I say this, 'lively tumors.' We've managed to curt the cliffedge with our experiments. Sure, the cells are revolting against the forced reconstitution efforts. But the compound is ... dynamic. Dr. ######## says it could be a catastrophe, a "world ending event".
Ha ... what an imagination.
The girl thinks this place wouldn't be qaurantined and pyro-glassed to high-hell before that even happens. Fret not I say, we are one of the most secure and advanced biogenetics firms in the known galaxy, the military in our pockets offers security and personnel unrivalled by our peers. Perks like administrative freedoms, enhanced emenities, and a security force that could vaporize an armada. Some talking tumors aren't going to stop us, no-- me, from achieving the glory that I deserve. I accused the girl of being a coward, "how did you even become a scientist? too busy sticking hypotheticals to paper and never practicing the practical element!"
Got a good laugh out of me, and Dr. Xeveye.
The others were too focused on their work to grasp my humor.

I guess I can't be too hard on the child. They've proven to have the technical ability. All that pencil-pushing made her accurate at least, and she managed to crack the first and second compound thresholds we needed for the serum.
If these idiots can maintain focus for a moment, we might actually finish this project within the projected time scope.
